idiom_name: hand-written emitter over std::fmt::Write (or quick-xml Writer)
implementation_notes: Rust's standard library has no markup support: the transformer is a function generic over std::fmt::Write (or std::io::Write) that writes escaped text with write!/write_str, which keeps output streaming and unit-testable against a String buffer. The quick-xml crate supplies an event-based Writer with optional serde serialization when XML structure matters, but there is no mainstream XSLT engine, so the declarative route is not practical. A per-format transformer trait remains useful when several formats must be emitted through one interface.
pitfalls: write! does not escape: every interpolated value needs the escape helper, or markup breaks and HTML becomes injectable.
std::fmt::Write reports failure as a bare fmt::Error and is not flushable; for I/O use std::io::Write and propagate io::Error instead.
quick-xml's Writer requires balanced start/end events and explicit escaping; event-ordering mistakes produce output that looks well-formed but is wrong.
